CRAS: alsa_jack - Separate jack_list creation and finding jacks Separate cras_alsa_jack_list_create into jack_list creation and finding jacks by name matching. Add fields card_name, card_index, direction to cras_alsa_jack_list so finding jacks can reuse those fields without passing parameters. Wrap the original usage into cras_alsa_jack_create_jack_list_and_find_jacks so cras_alsa_io can have least change. In the future changes, cras_alsa_io will go through one of the paths in alsa_iodev_create: - If FullySpecifiedUCM is enabled, call cras_alsa_jack_list_create to create a jack list, and find jacks by going through the sections with matched device name. CHROMIUM: ecryptfs: Have the kthread open the lower file under SELinux When SELinux is enabled, files are associated with the current task's SID when they are opened. Before this change, the lower file would sometimes be associated with the SID of the first process to open the corresponding eCryptfs file. If a second process attempts to access this file through the same lower file, the access is denied unless the SELinux policy allows the second process to use files opened by the first process (the FD__USE permission). Since it may not be desirable to allow all processes this permission, this change always opens the lower file from a thread with the kernel SID. This way, the policy only needs to grant all processes FD__USE on the kernel context (which in practice, is exactly the use of eCryptfs lower files). TEST=Built/ran Chrome OS/Android with SELinux enforcing. BUG=b:25408463 Change-Id: If22e125a48f474b7f0dfeb162bc77bd603431ba1 Signed-off-by: Ricky Zhou <rickyz@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/331397 Reviewed-by: Gwendal Grignou <gwendal@chromium.org>

CR50: handle big-endian RSA keys The TPM library serializes RSA keys in big-endian format, while CR50 requires little-endian. Handle endianness by converting from big to little and back to big within the _cpri__* layer. Also modify test code to make copies of static const RSA keys, as these get placed on read-only memory. [Reland] sshd: try to make ssh connection more reliable. Provisioning a new OS image shows many instances of ssh connections droped, like autoserv| Master ssh connection to w.x.y.z is down. autoserv| Starting master ssh connection Many of these are harmless. But even manually connecting to a DUT I get dropped connections, I think when the machine gets busy, but hasn't rebooted yet: packet_write_wait: Connection to w.x.y.z: Broken pipe Autotest currently connects to a DUT with the following options: ConnectTimeout=30 ServerAliveInterval=900 ServerAliveCountMax=3 ConnectionAttempts=4 Protocol=2 Basically it puts the burden of keeping the connection alive on the server controlling the DUT. Interestingly we do see failures after 900 seconds quite often, sometimes after 1350s. As the sampling is so coarse it is hard to say if this is just bad luck, bad network or a rebooted/dead machine. This change tries to make the DUT more cooperative by letting it ping the connection to the ssh client (autotest server) once a minute, ignoring all network errors for half a day (one hour would probably be enough but I see no harm in being generous). It does not change how autotest itself connects to the DUT. BUG=chromium:598517 TEST=Made a lars image, ssh to it. Change-Id: I1571a0b19d1ec2eb164151b36c11d0f73536d548 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/338898 Commit-Ready: Ilja Friedel <ihf@chromium.org> Tested-by: Ilja Friedel <ihf@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Haixia Shi <hshi@chromium.org>

checkpatch: suppress split string warnings By default checkpatch.pl warns about long lines even when for the lines including quoted string. Splitting the line in two also causes a warning, there is no way to avoid warning when long strings are present in the code. Adding another command line option suppresses the split string warning, and creates a way to avoid checkpatch warnings. Also sorted the options to make it easier to follow the list. BRANCH=none BUG=none TEST=verified that split strings do not cause warning any more.
